d: The pouch of Douglas: the peritoneal recess between the uterus and the rectum, resting on the posterior vaginal fornix. It is the lowest point of the female peritoneal cavity, so fluid collects there first.
The suspensory ligament of the ovary. This peritoneal fold runs from the ovary to the pelvic side wall and carries the ovarian artery and vein. The ureter lies just medial to it at the pelvic brim.

The connective tissue between the fascia lining the pelvic walls and the fascia wrapping the organs. It thickens into the cardinal, uterosacral and pubocervical ligaments, which support the cervix and upper vagina.
The distance from the sacral promontory to the lower edge of the pubic symphysis, measured on vaginal exam. Subtracting 1.5 to 2 cm estimates the obstetric conjugate, the true inlet diameter.
Parasympathetic nerves from S2 to S4 that join the inferior hypogastric plexus. They contract the detrusor, cause erection and supply the hindgut. Every other splanchnic nerve is sympathetic.

A network of valveless veins around the spine that connects with the pelvic, prostatic and breast veins. Flow reverses when abdominal pressure rises, so prostate, breast or uterine cancer can reach the spine without passing through the lungs.

Semen flowing backward into the bladder at orgasm because the internal urethral sphincter fails to close. It causes a dry orgasm and cloudy urine, and follows sympathetic nerve injury, bladder neck surgery or alpha-1 blockers.
